question.problem:
The time $t$ it took Noah to run $200\,\text{m}$ was $31.2\,\text{s}$ to the nearest tenth of a second. Determine the upper and lower bounds of this measurement.

{{field-1}}$\text{s}$
$\,\le t<$
{{field-2}}$\text{s}$
question.worked_solution:
Our measurement is given to the nearest $0.1\,\text{s}.$ So, the greatest possible error of this measurement is

$$
\frac{0.1\,\text{s}}{2}=0.05\,\text{s}.
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the lower and upper bounds of this measurement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{lower bound} & =31.2\,\text{s}-0.05\,\text{s} \\  & =31.15\,\text{s} \\ \text{upper bound} & =31.2\,\text{s}+0.05\,\text{s} \\  & =31.25\,\text{s}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the exact value of $t$ lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

$$
31.15\,\text{s}\le t<31.25\,\text{s}.
$$
